What Cedar keeps about you across conversations: a profile it reads before every reply, the facts and instructions you stated, past conversations and ways of working. Changes apply from your next message.
When you tell Cedar something lasting, like your name, a preference or a project, or ask it to remember something, it appears here.
This server doesn\'t remember anything between conversations yet. Update cedar to use memory.

Tap a memory to open the conversation it came from; long-press to pin, archive or delete it. Pinned memories are in every reply; archived ones leave Cedar\'s prompt and stay here until deleted. Memory stays on your own server and is never shared with a third party. Settings → Tools in the web UI turns it off.

resources.string: Data Cedar keeps for you across conversations, like a running log or weekly measurements, to compare with later. Deleting a set applies from your next message.
When you give Cedar data to come back to, like a weekly export or your measurements, it saves the rows here and can compare them week by week.
This server doesn\'t keep records between conversations yet. Update cedar to use records.
From a conversation not in this app
This set holds no rows yet.

Cedar is told each set\'s name, size and columns, never the rows, until it looks them up. Tap a set to see its rows; long-press to delete it. Records stay on your own server and are never shared with a third party. Settings → Tools in the web UI turns them off.

Your prompts, the agent\'s replies and tool calls, the system prompt and tool definitions it ran with, how the run ended, and the outcome you report.

Never: attached files and their names, your memory list, run and key identifiers, exact times, your region. Emails, phone and account numbers, IP addresses, keys and home-directory names become made-up stand-ins of the same shape, consistent within the conversation and random otherwise.
Conversations that used Gmail or Calendar can\'t be contributed. Redaction is best effort: the review is where you read for what it can\'t catch.
No account, no identity. A pseudonym, if you choose one, is a random id made on your server; you can rotate or drop it. You can withdraw a contribution below.
